This agreement displays only the lower-division courses required in the major. Although completion of the coursework listed below is not necessarily mandatory prior to admission, students are strongly advised to complete as much lower-division course preparation as possible prior to transfer. This agreement does not contain upper-division (junior-senior) major requirements, general education, or all-university requirements necessary for completion of this degree. In some cases, there may be alternative course options at the upper-division level. Please review the CSUSB catalog for full details.


TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION

You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students


TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY

Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx


FINANCIAL AID

Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award


ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer

Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines

Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units.


EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS

  • The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration


TEST CREDIT

If you took an AP, IB, or CLEP test, you can look up your CSUSB credit here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/test-credit


TRANSFER HELP

Do you have questions about your transfer work? Need some guidance? You can talk with one of our Transfer and Graduation Counselors!

  • Email: transferhelp@csusb.edu
  • Phone: 909-537-5200, Option 4
  • Zoom: Set up an appointment by emailing transferhelp@csusb.edu

You are also welcome to visit us in person. We are located in the Office of the Registrar, on the first floor of University Hall (interactive map link).

CONCENTRATIONS

Students in this major are required to chose one of the following concentrations:

  • Media Studies
  • Relational and Organizational Communication
  • Strategic Communication
  • Specialized


MAJOR INFORMATION

Communication and media shape the ways we understand and interact in our social worlds. The Bachelor of Arts in Communication degree helps students develop valuable communication understandings and skills through a deep, practical, timely, and relevant curriculum.


Five core courses expose students to major communication institutions and processes, theoretical perspectives and research techniques for studying those phenomena, and career pathways and ethical considerations for communication professionals. Students deepen these understandings and sharpen their skills by specializing in one of the program's concentrations. Furthermore, a wide range of Experiential Learning courses gives students real-life, hands-on experience in communication and media practices to prepare them for their careers, future study, and for wider life in general. Together, this mix of theory and practice prepares students for a lifetime of personal, civic, and professional communication, including careers in various fields, such as: human resources, training and development, management, leadership and coaching, journalism, broadcasting, filmmaking, digital/social media strategy and management, strategic communication for corporations, non-profits, and government entities; and many others. Many of our students also go on to study with Master’s degree programs and Ph.D. programs, including our own M.A. in Communication Studies: https://catalog.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/arts-letters/communication-studies/communication-studies-ma/. Often our M.A. students and those who go on to attain doctoral degrees become teachers in schools or lecturers and tenured faculty at community colleges and four-year universities in California and across the United States.


Students are required to choose one of the four concentrations within the B.A. in Communication: Media Studies, Relational and Organizational Communication, Strategic Communication, or the Specialized Concentration.

To be eligible for the Specialized Concentration, students must complete a proposal for their program plan, including all the communication courses that they intend to take in the concentration and a rationale for the course of study. The proposal will be reviewed by a Communication Studies faculty advisor before a student can be approved for this concentration. Before declaring this concentration, a student must have completed the following core classes: COMM 2101, COMM 3101, and COMM 3102. Only 9 units of Communication Studies course work completed prior to such approval can be applied toward the Specialized Concentration.


For more information about the Department of Communication Studies, please visit: https://www.csusb.edu/communication-studies

A short video featuring our students and their family members explaining what Communication Studies is all about: https://youtu.be/f86rbL60CHw

Students are welcome to email the department at: commstudies@csusb.edu


ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS

The complete list of major requirements is available here: https://bulletin.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/arts-letters/communication-studies/communication-ba/


ARTICULATION AGREEMENT NOTES

**Experiential Learning Requirement (Practicum Courses):

Students choose six units from at least two of the following experiential learning courses. In these courses, students apply Communication theories and practices in supervised, \"hands-on\" activities, and they reflect on those experiences. Students can only apply six experiential learning units toward the B.A. in Communication; however, additional experiential learning units may contribute to a minor (where applicable), or to a student's general graduation requirements (120 units). Experiential learning courses may not be used as elective units, either in the B.A. in Communication or its respective concentrations.


**Major Electives:

In addition to the Communication core, experiential learning, and concentration coursework, students choose six elective units in COMM coursework to broaden and deepen their understandings of communication processes. Three of the six elective units must be upper division. Students can only apply six elective units toward the B.A. in Communication; however, additional elective units may contribute to a minor (where applicable), or to a student's general graduation requirements (120 units). COMM 1000, 1002, 1006, and 1007 (or their transfer equivalents) may not be applied toward the B.A. in Communication. Possible lower-division courses are listed for this requirement area - students may petition the department to substitute others. Courses may not count for both the Major Electives and the Concentration.


CSUSB ADVISING PODCASTS

Find out more about this major here:

  • What is the Communication Studies Major?


ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

The following concentrations in this major are similar to the Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT) in Communication Studies: Media Studies, Relational and Organizational Communication, and Strategic Communication.

The concentration in Media Studies is also similar to the ADT in Film, TV & Electronic Media.


Completion of the ADT guarantees that students will be able to graduate from a similar-designated major at CSUSB in no more than 60 semester units. The ADT does not guarantee that all lower-division requirements are met.


Community college transfer students with a compatible ADT MUST meet with an academic advisor early in their first term and each subsequent term to stay on track for graduation.
